Two Pointers.kid: Imagine a long line of kids sorted from shortest to tallest. You stand at the short end and a friend stands at the tall end. To find two kids whose heights add up to a number, you both walk towards each other: if the pair is too short, you step up; if it's too tall, your friend steps down. You never need to check every pair.
when: Find a pair / triplet with a target sum

Sliding Window.kid: Think of a window frame you slide along a train. You only look at what is inside the frame. When the train moves one step, one new carriage comes into view on the right and one leaves on the left, so you update your count instead of re-counting every carriage.
when: Longest / shortest / best contiguous subarray or substring
Fixed size k window (max sum of k elements)
Condition like 'at most k distinct' or 'no repeats'

Fast and Slow Pointer.kid: Two kids run around a circular track. One runs twice as fast. If the track is a loop they will definitely meet again; if it's a straight road the fast one just reaches the end. Meeting means 'there is a loop'. And when the fast kid finishes a straight road, the slow kid is exactly in the middle.
when: Find the middle of a list

Reversal of Linked List.kid: A row of kids each holds the hand of the kid in front. To reverse the row, every kid lets go and grabs the hand of the kid behind instead. You do it one kid at a time, remembering who is next before letting go.
when: Reverse a linked list or a part of it
Reverse nodes in groups of k

Modified Binary Search.kid: I'm thinking of a number from 1 to 100. You guess 50 and I say 'higher'. Now you only need to look at 51 to 100, so you guess 75. Every guess throws away half of the possibilities, so even a million numbers take only about 20 guesses.
when: 'Find the minimum X such that ...' (search on the answer)
Anything where a yes/no check flips from false to true once

Prefix Sum.kid: You have a long row of piggy banks and a friend keeps asking 'how many coins from box 3 to box 8?'. Instead of counting each time, you first write on every box 'total so far'. Now the answer is just one subtraction: total at 8 minus total at 2.
when: Count subarrays with a property (use a map of prefix sums)

Hash Map.kid: Think of a coat check. You hand over a coat and get a numbered ticket. Later you show the ticket and the attendant finds the coat at once, without searching every hook. A hash map is that magic ticket desk for your data.
when: Need to know 'have I seen this before?'

Monotonic Stack.kid: Kids line up for a photo and each one wants to know 'who is the first taller kid behind me?'. A kid stands on a pile of shorter kids; when a taller kid arrives, all the shorter ones learn their answer and leave the pile. The pile always stays in order of height.

Overlapping Intervals.kid: Each kid has a play-time slot, like 2pm-4pm. To see who clashes, line the kids up by start time. If the next kid starts before the current kid finishes, they overlap, so you merge their slots into one longer slot.
when: Meeting rooms (can one person attend all?)

Cyclic Sort.kid: You have kids with jersey numbers 1 to N standing in random spots, and each number has a matching seat. Each kid just goes to the seat that matches their number, swapping with whoever is sitting there. In the end, any seat with the wrong kid shows exactly which number is missing.

Matrix Manipulation.kid: A chocolate bar is a grid of squares. To eat it in a spiral, you go along the top row, down the right side, back along the bottom and up the left, then repeat on the smaller bar that is left. To spin a photo, you swap the corner pieces around, layer by layer.

Breadth First Search (BFS).kid: Drop a stone in a pond. The ripples spread out ring by ring: first everything one step away, then everything two steps away. BFS visits places in exactly this order, so the first time it reaches your target is the shortest way there.
when: Shortest path in an unweighted graph or grid
Level order traversal of a tree

Depth First Search (DFS).kid: You are in a maze with a ball of string. You walk down one corridor as far as you can; at a dead end you follow the string back to the last fork and try the next corridor. You explore everything behind one door completely before trying the next door.
when: Anything recursive on a grid or graph

Trees.kid: A family tree: one grandparent at the top, children below, grandchildren below them. Most tree questions are answered by asking each child the same question and then combining their answers: 'how tall are you?' ... 'I'm the tallest child's height plus one'.

Graphs.kid: Friends on a playground, with some holding hands. A graph is just 'who is connected to whom'. Questions are like: can the message get from Asha to Ravi through friends? Is there a circle of friends? In what order must we put on socks, then shoes, then shoes' laces?

Backtracking.kid: You are choosing an outfit: a shirt, then trousers, then shoes. If the shoes clash, you don't throw the outfit away entirely; you take the shoes off and try other ones, and if nothing works you go back and change the trousers. Try, check, undo, try something else.
when: Any 'find all valid ...' with choices at each step

Greedy.kid: You have a bag of coins and want to pay 63 rupees with as few coins as possible. You grab the biggest coin that still fits, again and again. You never undo a choice. It works when taking the best thing right now can never hurt you later.
when: Sorting by some ratio, then picking

Dynamic Programming.kid: To count the stairs to the top you ask: 'how many ways to reach the step below me and the step two below me?' and add them. Instead of re-counting the same steps again and again, you write each answer on a sticky note and look it up next time. Big problem = small problems + sticky notes.
when: Count the ways / min cost / max profit
Choices at each step with overlapping sub-problems
Knapsack, LIS, LCS, edit distance, coin change

Bitwise XOR.kid: XOR is a magic switch: flip a light twice and it is back to how it started. If every kid in a room has a twin who flips the same switch, all the lights cancel out and only the kid without a twin leaves the switch changed.
when: Swap or flip bits, count set bits

Top K Elements.kid: A talent show picks the 3 best singers. You keep a small podium with only 3 spots. Each new singer is compared with the weakest person on the podium; if they are better, they replace that person. At the end the podium holds the top 3 without sorting everybody.

K-way Merge.kid: K queues of kids, each already sorted by height. A teacher wants one sorted line. She looks only at the first kid of each queue, takes the shortest, and then looks at the new first kid of that queue. Repeat until all queues are empty.
when: Kth smallest in a sorted matrix
Find K pairs with smallest sums

Two Heaps.kid: To always know the middle kid in a growing line, split the kids into a 'shorter half' and a 'taller half'. The tallest of the short half and the shortest of the tall half sit at the middle, so the median is always one of those two - and you can see them without sorting.
Two Heaps.time: O(log n) per add, O(1) median

Design Data Structure.kid: You are building your own toy box with special rules, like 'the toy I touched last is easiest to grab' (LRU cache) or 'find any toy that starts with ca...' (a trie). You pick two simple boxes that are good at different things and wire them together so every operation is fast.
when: Insert / delete / get random in O(1)
